acceptance_criteria.description: Given MCPHOST_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL points at a test server, When signups are paused via the pause file, Then within 30s the server receives one POST with key: "signup.paused" and the alerts row has delivery_status: "delivered".
Given the pause alert was raised 10s ago, When the pause toggles again inside the cooldown, Then no second POST is sent and the open row's repeat_count is 1.
Given a tenant whose calls_per_day trips 20 times within 5 min, When the 20th trip occurs, Then one quota.trip alert exists for that tenant and plan knob; the 21st trip raises nothing new.
Given 100 calls in 5 min of which 6 return 5xx-class errors, When the minute tick runs, Then one errors.rate alert is raised with the rate in the body; at 4 errors nothing is raised.
Given the webhook server returns 503 three times, When delivery runs, Then three retries occur at the documented backoff, delivery_status is "failed", and the host keeps serving tool calls.
Given MCPHOST_ALERT_TENANT is set, When any alert is raised, Then that tenant's host.msg.inbox returns a message from the system sender with the alert title and id.
Given three raised alerts, When admin.alerts.list {unacked_only: true} is called, Then all three return; after admin.alerts.ack {id} on one, the list returns two and admin_audit holds the ack entry.
Given both sink env vars unset, When an alert is raised, Then it is stored, nothing is sent, and healthz shows alerts.sink: "store-only".
Given MCPHOST_ALERT_MIN_SEVERITY=critical, When a warn alert is raised, Then it is stored and not delivered; a critical one is delivered.
Given the host is running, When GET /healthz is called with the operator header, Then the body includes alerts.open and alerts.last_raised_at.
Given admin.alerts.raise is called with a body of 64 KiB, When it runs, Then it is rejected with a size error at 16 KiB and stored at 15 KiB.

Given prod after land, When the operator toggles the pause file on mcphost-1 and toggles it back, Then two alerts (signup.paused, signup.resumed) arrive at the configured sink and admin.alerts.list shows both (Live).

five_whys_trace.q: Why build alerting now, rather than continuing to rely on a human polling healthz?
five_whys_trace.a: The readiness plan lists 'alerting' as absent (wiki 2026-09-23-mcphost-market-test-plan) and the nightly measure has been RED for twelve runs without a page; the 2026-09-24 v0.60.5 deploy rolled back twice on Caddy 429s and nobody knew until a carbon session read the journal hours later. A Show HN wave with no alerting means the first report of an outage is a public comment, not an operator page.

five_whys_trace.q: Why collapse duplicate alerts per key into a cooldown window instead of raising one row per occurrence?
five_whys_trace.a: Goals: 'every host-visible failure class produces exactly one alert per key per cooldown' -- a tenant tripping its call quota 50 times in five minutes should page the operator once, not fifty times (User stories); repeat_count on the open row keeps the count visible without re-delivering.

five_whys_trace.q: Why deliver through a webhook POST and the host's own inbox rather than requiring a third-party paging account?
five_whys_trace.a: Goals: 'delivery works with no third-party account: a webhook URL and the host's own inbox' -- mcphost-1 has no PagerDuty/Opsgenie integration today, and host.msg already exists (PRD-mcphost-webhook-inbox); reusing it costs no new infrastructure.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does storage happen synchronously on the request path while delivery runs as a background task, rather than both being synchronous or both backgrounded?
five_whys_trace.a: Non-functional requirement: 'raising an alert never blocks the request path longer than 5ms (storage is synchronous, delivery is a background task); delivery failures never crash the host' -- a slow or down webhook target must never make an unrelated tool call (e.g. the one that trips quota.trip) itself slow or fail.

five_whys_trace.q: Why let MCPHOST_ALERT_MIN_SEVERITY filter delivery but never storage?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 7's own wording is explicit on this point, and AC9 proves it: an operator who raises the delivery bar to `critical` to cut webhook noise still wants every `warn` alert visible in `admin.alerts.list` afterward -- filtering storage too would silently lose the record of what happened, not just quiet the page.
